summary: The Literature depth (35 units of ENGLISH courses, at most one creative writing workshop) applies only to a student with no subplan, as the policies say ("choose between completing the Literature depth in discipline or completing one subplan"); every course must be letter graded with a C or better (the two CR/NC electives the Director of Undergraduate Studies may allow are moved in by hand), and a course counts toward one requirement only, so the WIM and capstone courses do not also count as electives. Prose and poetry are alternative Creative Writing concentrations with a 40-unit subplan minimum, and the subplans' electives are encoded. Courses on department-website lists stay checked by hand. The one-workshop cap covers every creative writing workshop number (ENGLISH 90-92, 190-192, 290-292 and their lettered versions), every elective rule takes courses of 3 units or more, and honors, once chosen, requires ENGLISH 196A and 197 with an A- or better on the essay, which also fill the capstone.

Dio0Xkt6.why: "35 units of approved courses, only one of which may be a creative writing course, chosen from those offered by the Department of English ... Courses must be taken for at least three units." The one upper-division foreign literature course allowed in place of an elective is not on any list; it is moved in by hand. The creative writing cap covers every workshop in the department's 90-92, 190-192 and 290-292 series (and ENGLISH 94), not only the base numbers: ENGLISH 190A or 192A is as much a creative writing course as ENGLISH 190.
